meta.task: Create a first issue, then find it again from My issues or Inbox
meta.taskDetail: One issue titled "Add CSV export to the reports page", created with the dialog's defaults, then looked up the way a new user would: My issues first, then Inbox.
meta.success: The new issue is found again from My issues or Inbox.
meta.firstValue: The issue just created shows up in a list of my work.
meta.startingState: The user's own Chrome, signed in to the workspace Myapptesting with one team (MYA). The user signed up and named the workspace before the walk; those screens were not captured. The workspace inbox holds onboarding issues closed by Linear 5 and 6 months earlier, so this is not a first-day workspace.
meta.environment: Chrome 155 in the user's own profile, 1440 × 900 at 2×, macOS, English UI, dark theme. Driven by Playwright over the browser's remote debugging connection.
meta.auditType: One task, AI-assisted. The rest of the product is out of scope.
meta.statusNote: The issue was found, but only in the Created tab of My issues; the Assigned tab, where My issues opens, showed no issues.

keep.text: Creating the issue is short: one click opens a dialog with the cursor in the title, and Create issue saves it. Title typed and saved in 4 interactions.
The confirmation names the result: a toast with the issue ID MYA-5, the title as a link, and buttons to copy the URL, ID and branch name.

summary.cutNote: Nothing in this flow qualifies. Every step was needed to finish the task.

change.text: When Assigned is empty, point to the issues the user created that nobody is assigned to. Right now the new issue is missing from the tab My issues opens on, and nothing says where it went.
Name what the display options hide ("2 canceled issues") instead of sending the user into a panel of eleven settings.

next.text: Ask five new users to create an issue and then find it. Note where they look first and whether they assign themselves. That shows whether the fix for finding 1 belongs in the empty state or in the default assignee.

findings.title: A new issue has no assignee by default, so it is missing from My issues, which opens on Assigned
findings.observed: In the Create issue dialog the assignee button reads "Assignee", described as "Currently no one is assigned" (step 4). The issue was saved with that default as MYA-5. My issues opens on the Assigned tab, which reads "No matching issues" and "2 issues hidden by display options" (step 6). MYA-5 is listed only under the Created tab (step 8). The Assigned empty state does not mention MYA-5 or the Created tab.
findings.matters: Finding the issue again is the second half of the task. The product's own name for the list, My issues, and its default tab both lead away from the issue the user just made, and the empty state blames display options instead of the missing assignee.
findings.hypothesis: New users decide the issue was not saved, or create it again. Not observed with real users.
findings.recommendation: When Assigned is empty and the user created unassigned issues, say so in the empty state: "You created MYA-5. It isn't assigned to anyone." with Assign to me and View created. A reasonable designer could prefer making the creator the default assignee in a workspace with one member; that changes team behaviour, so test it before shipping.
findings.evidence: Dialog defaults and list contents read from the DOM at steps 4, 6 and 8. One automated run.

findings.title: The empty state says issues are hidden by display options but not which option or which issues
findings.observed: The Assigned tab reads "2 issues hidden by display options" with a Show options button (step 6). The button opens a panel with grouping, sub-grouping, ordering, completed issues set to "Past day", sub-issue settings and eleven display properties (step 7). No setting is marked as the one hiding the issues. The Inbox lists two onboarding issues, MYA-4 and MYA-2, both Canceled and closed by Linear (step 9).
findings.matters: The note explains the empty list with a cause the user did not set and cannot find. It also pulls attention to filters at the moment the real cause is the missing assignee in finding 1.
findings.hypothesis: The two hidden issues are the canceled onboarding issues, hidden by the completed-issues window. Inferred from the inbox, not confirmed in the list.
findings.recommendation: Name the cause in the note, for example "2 canceled issues hidden. Show", and let one click reveal them without opening the panel.
findings.evidence: Note text and panel settings read from the DOM at steps 6 and 7; inbox rows at step 9.

findings.title: The workspace opens on an agent chat, and issue creation is an unlabelled 28 px icon
findings.observed: After sign-in the workspace opens on "New chat" with "Introducing Linear Agent", a message box "Ask Linear…" and a notice "Linear Agent is now your default view" with Change and Keep (step 3). The only visible way to create an issue is a 28 × 28 px icon with no text label next to the workspace name. Clicking it opened the Create issue dialog (step 4).
findings.matters: This did not block the task: one click on the icon worked. It is noted because the first screen promotes asking the agent over creating an issue directly, and a user who wants to make an issue has to recognise the icon.
findings.hypothesis: Some new users type the issue into the agent chat instead. Not observed.
findings.recommendation: No change needed for this task. If the agent view stays the default for new workspaces, consider a labelled New issue entry on that screen.
findings.evidence: Icon size read from the DOM at step 3.

diagnosis.text: Finding 1 is partly a product question. Should a new issue belong to its creator by default? In a team that means noise in everyone's list; alone, it means issues that vanish from My issues. The answer depends on how workspaces grow from one member to many, which the interface cannot show.
